children: will be announcing earnings results this Monday after market close. Here’s what investors should know.

Zoom beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $1.28 billion, up 4.9% year on year. It was a mixed quarter for the company, with a solid beat of analysts’ billings estimates but adjusted operating income in line with analysts’ estimates. It added 91 enterprise customers paying more than $100,000 annually to reach a total of 4,625.
Is Zoom a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Zoom’s revenue to grow 4% year on year, in line with the 4.4% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Zoom has a history of exceeding Wall Street’s expectations.

Looking at Zoom’s peers in the video conferencing segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. 8x8 delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 4.3%, beating analysts’ expectations by 2.4%, and RingCentral reported revenues up 5.9%, topping estimates by 1.3%. 8x8’s stock price was unchanged after the resultswhile RingCentral was up 5%.

In the last twelve months or so, the market has shifted its attention from one area of macro importance to the next (AI disintermediation and AI capex spending to geopolitical conflict, rates, and whether the economy is on solid footing or not). While some of the video conferencing stocks have shown solid performance in this choppy environment, the group has generally underperformed, with share prices down 13.2% on average over the last month. Zoom is down 14.6% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $118.52 (compared to the current share price of $81.75).
